thread:
aj: canary #135 (eu) showing 4x latency and ~5% 5xx, looks like we need to unwind. proposing quick-unwind: ramp traffic back to main, safe eviction of canary session keys, and purge model-specific caches. any objections?
maria: do we have sticky sessions for that route? if yes we need a drain window or we'll flip active users mid-request.
sam: yes cookie affinity. I suggest staged ramp: canary -> 10% -> 0% over 60s to let in-flight requests finish. console has fast-revert but that instant switch will break sessions if we don't handle KV.
aj: console shows two rollback modes in UI (fast revert / safe disable). fast revert is tempting for immediate mitigation but worried about cache fallout. ops thoughts?
nate: fast revert swaps router target immediately. If we do that, must invalidate model-specific caches and session routing keys for canary. keys to consider: `canary:v2:session:*` and `kv-cache:prompt-hash:canary-v2:*`. Quick evict example:
```
redis-cli --scan --pattern "kv-cache:prompt-hash:canary-v2:*" | xargs -n100 redis-cli del
```
but deleting session keys will drop users. prefer TTL approach if we want graceful.
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered rollback_preflight check: runbook 7.4 matched. no blocking infra issues.
maria: agree with TTL approach — set short TTL on session routing keys so users expire off the canary naturally, then remove the route. avoids mass logout. TTL update snippet:
```
for k in $(redis-cli --scan --pattern "canary:v2:session:*"); do redis-cli expire "$k" 30; done
```
sam: and only delete the model cache (prompt-hash) after traffic is 0%. chat transcripts should remain untouched. we should avoid deleting any user-generated history keys.
aj: proposed sequence:
1) set canary traffic -> 0% via routing API (or ramp to 0 with short steps)
2) set TTL 60s on `canary:v2:session:*` keys to let affinity drain
3) wait 90s and confirm via metrics (inflight requests near 0)
4) remove canary routing rule from config
5) purge `kv-cache:prompt-hash:canary-v2:*` caches
Code (single-shot):
```
# step 1
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://console.redwood/api/admin/traffic" -d '{"route":"canary-v2","pct":0}'
# step 2 TTL job
for k in $(redis-cli --scan --pattern "canary:v2:session:*"); do redis-cli expire "$k" 60; done
# step 5 purge lists
redis-cli --scan --pattern "kv-cache:prompt-hash:canary-v2:*" | xargs -n100 redis-cli del
```
nate: also annotate the rollout/incident so automated rollouts won't try to reapply the canary: `rollout annotate <id> rollback:canary-v2` and mute the rollout alert group for 10m.
maria: :thumbsup: I'll run the TTL job now. @sam can you prepare the purge script but hold on delete until I confirm 0% traffic? @nate please mute alerts.
sam: purge script ready, will test on staging keys first and hold.
aj: executing plan now. deploy-bot please add an annotation "rollback:canary-v2" and tag related alerts.
deploy-bot: rollback action started by aj. traffic set to 0% for canary-v2. annotation added: rollback:canary-v2.
ops-bot: monitoring update: within 2m 5xx rate dropped ~52%, latencies back to baseline. leaving alert group muted for 15m.
aj: thanks everyone. follow-up: improve console UX to offer a one-click "rollback + safe-evict" that runs this sequence and adds annotation. filing a ticket after postmortem.
